title: UK-Iranian dual national arrested over RAF Fairford investigation bailed
description: A UK-Iranian dual national arrested on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts in connection with an incident at RAF Fairford has been released on
body: A UK-Iranian dual national arrested on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts in connection with an incident at RAF Fairford has been released on bail.The 25-year-old man was arrested in the London borough of Westminster on Thursday. Searches of two properties in the same area have now finished. A major incident was declared and dozens of homes were evacuated after police were alerted to three "suspicious vehicles" near the airbase in Gloucestershire last weekend.Five other men in their twenties were arrested and were subsequently released on police bail. All five were UK nationals from London.The investigation into the circumstances surrounding the events are continuing, police said.Last weekend, the five men aged between 23 and 25 were arrested in the early hours of the morning after vehicles were reported to be travelling towards the base operated by the US Air Force (USAF), sparking a major security incident.The BBC understands that one of the men had dialled 999 himself, about an hour before a local farmer alerted police to a "large group" of masked men near the vehicles.They were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences and later on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, before being released on bail on Monday in what police called an "investigative decision" that was "grounded in experience and strategy".Prime Minister Andy Burnham chaired a Cobra meeting that afternoon in response. He later said there were "strong indications" that Iran had played a part in the incident, but did not provide any more details.Tehran has strongly denied any involvement. The Iranian embassy in London said on Monday that it "categorically rejects and strongly condemns" what it called "unfounded and malicious speculations" linking Iran to the incident.RAF Fairford has been used as a forward operating location by the US Air Force (USAF) for decades.In recent months, US bombers have taken off from the base for the Middle East, after the UK approved a US request to use it for defensive strikes on Iran.In July, Iran said "any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces".Late on Monday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told a TV show that it was clear a "foreign actor" had been involved in events over the weekend.Without providing evidence or giving further details, he told Fox News network's "Hannity" programme: "What happened, what almost happened, what could have happened in the UK over the weekend is a very serious situation. It's one that clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor."Speaking earlier at the Oval Office, US President Donald Trump said he would not have let the five men arrested out on bail, and that he was "surprised" they had been released."We know everything about them, we would not have released them," he said, adding that the UK had worked with the US "very closely" on this.

schema.headline: UK-Iranian dual national arrested over RAF Fairford investigation bailed

title: Man shot dead in East Acton as people gather for memorial service
description: A murder investigation has been launched after a 40-year-old man was shot dead in a "senseless act of violence" as up to 50 people – including childre
body: A murder investigation has been launched after a 40-year-old man was shot dead in a "senseless act of violence" as up to 50 people – including children – gathered for a memorial service in west London.The Met Police said it was called to the scene at 19:47 GMT on Friday after multiple shots had been heard by members of the public at the junction of Braybrook Street and Erconwald Street in East Acton.Officers attended alongside the London Ambulance Service but the man was pronounced dead at the scene, despite the efforts of medics.No arrests have been made and a police cordon remains in place in Braybrook Street. Police are appealing for witnesses to come forward.The victim's family have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers.A post-mortem examination is scheduled to establish the cause of death, but the victim is believed to have sustained a gunshot wound, the force said.Det Ch Insp Brian Howie, who is leading the investigation, said: "Our thoughts are with the family and friends of a man whose life was taken in a senseless act of violence."We understand a large number of people had gathered for a memorial service and what should have been a time to come together in remembrance has instead left a family devastated."We believe between 40 and 50 people, including children, were present when this incident occurred. Someone knows what happened and we need them to come forward."He has asked anyone who was around Erconwald Street, Braybrook Street, the surrounding roads or Wormwood Scrubs playground between 18:00 and 20:00, to "please think carefully about what you saw". He added: "Did you see anyone carrying or concealing weapons, people on bicycles acting suspiciously, or vehicles being driven at speed?"We also want to hear from anyone with photographs, video, dashcam, doorbell or mobile phone footage or who has seen anything relevant on social media."However insignificant it may seem, the smallest piece of information could prove crucial in helping us establish what happened and identify those responsible."Listen to the best of BBC Radio London on Sounds and follow BBC London on Facebook,, external X,, external and Instagram., external Send your story ideas to hello.bbclondon@bbc.co.uk

title: Bahrain GP in Malaysia 2026: Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1
description: Even Lewis Hamilton, starting from his equal best grid position of the year in second place, fears Max Verstappen will be tough to beat in Sunday's Ba
body: Even Lewis Hamilton, starting from his equal best grid position of the year in second place, fears Max Verstappen will be tough to beat in Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.Verstappen has dominated the weekend so far on Formula 1's return to the Sepang track for the first time since 2017.Hamilton joins him on the front row to revive memories of their no-holds-barred title battle five years ago.But at nearly 0.3 seconds slower in qualifying, and with the pace Verstappen has shown all weekend, Hamilton's mindset on Saturday was to "just try my best to hold on to him tomorrow".This was Verstappen's first pole position of the year - a remarkable statistic for someone who came within two points of winning a fifth world title last year after one of the all-time great fightbacks.Red Bull started the year off the pace - the car was on average more than 0.5secs a lap slower than Mercedes in the first half of the year - and for a time there were questions as to whether Verstappen would stick around for 2027.But after being courted by McLaren, Verstappen signed a two-year contract extension over the summer break, saying he believed in the Red Bull project and didn't mind putting in the work to turn things around. Verstappen arrived in Malaysia after a run of three consecutive podium finishes, and with Red Bull hoping to prove out an upgrade that had seen them finish less than 0.2secs off victory in Baku last Sunday.In the tropical heat of Malaysia, around the demanding long corners of this track with perhaps the roughest surface of the season, the upgrade - centred on a new floor - has more than proved its worth."It's been an incredible result for us," Verstappen said. "Looking at the season, how it started for us and the progression that we have made. At some tracks we were kind of close, but now I think this weekend it was very positive for us."We have been adding bits to the car and they have worked. It's simple as that. When they work, you gain lap time, you have a better overall balance in the car."So with tyres that are very sensitive to balance, that gives you also more lap time."And then on a track probably where it's all very hot and you want a, let's say, stable balance or connected balance, then that's very important. And that's what we have found a little bit more over the last weekends."Hamilton, for one, but also Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli, who under-performed slightly in qualifying because of a combination between an unusual tyre strategy and an error on an early run.The world championship leader's fourth place becomes third on the grid with Hadjar's penalty, and he can usually be relied upon to be a factor in the race.Antonelli's main focus will be his advantage over team-mate George Russell, who trails the Italian by 66 points and starts four places behind, his momentum from his Baku win stalled, and somewhat perplexed as to his and his team's lack of pace.At Mercedes, the bigger question is over the aerodynamic upgrade they brought to the car this weekend.Mercedes are lagging behind their rivals when it comes to developing their car this season, apparently at least in part because they front-loaded their spend early in the season.But this first big update since the Canadian Grand Prix in June has not yet proved the step they had expected.The question is whether that is to do with the parts themselves or the very specific conditions of this weekend, in the heat and on the rough track surface, which is putting the tyres through the mill, and massively limiting the useful laps teams can do in terms of set-up work.Antonelli said: "With this new package, obviously the window of the way the car operates is different. So, we're trying to understand in which window the car performance is best, in the high-speed corner and low-speed corners."Our high-speed performance has been very strong this weekend. We were very quick in the high-speed, but in the low-speed we lacked. So, we need to understand why and try to move on and improve."As for the race, Antonelli said: "Track position is going to be very important. Strategy is going to be really important."It's a race where we will attack. Because undercut (stopping first and gaining time on a rival on fresh tyres) is incredibly powerful."So whenever there's an opportunity, we should go for maybe an undercut and try to maximise our opportunity."Tomorrow might be two stops, three stops. We don't know. But the only thing we know is that it's going to be roasting hot out there."

schema.headline: Bahrain GP in Malaysia 2026: Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1

title: Russia hits second major bridge in Ukraine's capital Kyiv
description: A Russian strike has hit a second major bridge in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko has said, as Moscow ramps up attacks on critical infrastructure in Ukr
body: A Russian strike has hit a second major bridge in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko has said, as Moscow ramps up attacks on critical infrastructure in Ukraine's capital.The attack on Saturday morning injured two people, and damaged the road surface and overhead trolleybus wires on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge, Klitschko said, causing traffic jams.It comes after the Pivdennyi (Southern) Bridge was hit multiple times by Russian drones this week, with Klitschko warning that "the enemy is tearing Kyiv apart".Russia said its drones had hit the two bridges used to transfer Ukrainian troops and military cargo. Moscow again urged foreign citizens, including diplomats, to leave Kyiv. The two Kyiv bridges across the Dnipro River link the western and eastern parts of the capital and had not been hit before Thursday.The Russian strikes have severed road, rail and trolleybus links across the wide river. The ongoing drone threat means restrictions on other routes, bringing traffic jams to the city's roads for a second day - though Friday's gridlock has not been repeated to the same level.Many of the city's residents - which number about three million - rely on the metro to travel across the city every day. The fear is this new Russian tactic will result in sustained attacks which could effectively cut the city in two.Writing on Telegram on Saturday morning, Klitschko said "emergency services are on their way" after the Pivnichnyi Bridge was hit."Traffic on the bridge from the left to the right bank is currently blocked," he added.Earlier attacks on the Pivdennyi Bridge prompted Kyiv's defence council to hold a crisis meeting on Friday. Klitschko warned afterwards that the city was now in a "very dramatic situation" as Moscow was battering its "critical infrastructure, logistics, housing" and other key facilities.Experts say Russian drones are unlikely to bring down the bridges - but repeated attacks will force their closure and risk weakening their structure, making them unusable. More powerful weapons could collapse the bridges, some of which are reported to be in poor condition after years carrying heavier traffic than they were designed for.It was reported that Ukrainian lawmakers discussed the state of Kyiv's bridges in a recent meeting, setting out contingency plans to use ferries or temporary pontoon bridges to keep the city connected in the event of any bridges being destroyed.Russian President Vladimir Putin has said Russia is acting in response to Ukraine's strikes on Russian energy facilities, despite the fact that it was Moscow that had first launched such attacks.After the Pivdennyi Bridge was attacked, passengers described how dust from a blast wave entered their carriage through the ventilation system.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Putin had decided that there were "no rules now" when attacking Ukraine. In an interview with the Financial Times, he said: "The Russians have failed to occupy us. So now they are carrying out massive attacks and mass killings."He added: "They want to destroy our bridges... our data centres, the internet, mobile networks, hospitals, kindergartens, schools, universities - everything. They want people to flee their cities."Putin on Thursday insisted that Russia's attacks on Ukrainian economic targets were a direct response to Ukraine's strikes on Russia's oil refineries and its ships in the Black Sea."Now from every direction we're receiving calls 'let's stop'. But they started it," Putin said after a wide-ranging speech at the Valdai foreign policy forum.The Kremlin leader admitted Kyiv had "got some results" from its refinery attacks and Russia had lost about 1% of its GDP. Ukraine maintains it began attacking Russian oil infrastructure because it helps the Kremlin finance the war.Russia has targeted Ukrainian energy infrastructure, ramping up attacks every winter since Putin launched a full-scale invasion in February 2022.

schema.headline: Russia hits second major bridge in Ukraine's capital Kyiv

title: Spoilers: Is social media ruining gig surprises?
description: Spoiler alert! Is social media ruining big gig surprises? Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Big moments from Olivia Rodrigo's tour were dissect
body: Spoiler alert! Is social media ruining big gig surprises? Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Big moments from Olivia Rodrigo's tour were dissected online shortly after her opening night BySrosh Khan and Riyah CollinsBBC NewsbeatMonths before you have a chance to see your favourite artist, chances are you already know some of the big moments they have planned.  You'll also probably know the set list, the stage design, and - if you've really been paying attention - where to stand to get the best view. When it comes to films and TV series, spoilers tend to be guarded against with warnings.But for many major gigs, there's no escaping a stream of fan videos from the shows if you're online, whether you like it or not.Last week, US pop star Olivia Rodrigo kicked off her Unraveled tour, and surprises from the show, which scores of fans have paid a lot of money to see, have already been dissected online.Tours by Harry Styles, Charli XCX and Ariana Grande have also been filmed from every angle and shared over the past few months.While some fans lap up the opportunity to see what's coming, others are taking extreme measures to preserve the element of surprise. Image source, HandoutImage caption, Aurélia Collins always aims to go to gigs not knowing what to expectAurélia Collins is one of them, spending weeks trying to trick her algorithm into not serving her content about her favourite artists and tapping "not interested" when videos come up, even though she says "it hurts my soul". It can mean her social media feed is a bit bland, but she tells BBC Newsbeat "it's worth it for the surprise".The 20-year-old criminology student is a huge One Direction fan and says she just about managed to avoid spoilers for Styles' Together, Together tour over summer. But when one slipped through the net about Niall Horan before she was able to see his show in London on Saturday - her first time seeing him live after being a fan for 16 years - she was "gutted"."When I was younger, we couldn't afford to go to events like this and hear live music and because it's such a moment, I really want to take it in," she says."I want the full experience, and that includes the element of surprise that people that go to the opening night of the tour can get."Image source, HandoutImage caption, Georgia McAdam says videos online help her plan her gig experience Not all fans think spoilers are a bad thing, though. In fact, Georgia McAdam claims she loves them."I'm the type of person that loves to be prepared," the 22-year-old says. "I love to know what the stage is looking like, what the set list consists of and where to stand."McAdam's a huge Olivia Rodrigo fan and sees online spoilers more as "teasers". She feels no amount of online videos can ever really take away from the excitement of the real thing. "Sometimes you get different surprise songs to what's online or you never know what an artist might do," she adds.'You have to not look at TikTok'Some artists have reacted by switching up their sets in small ways each night to make sure fans coming to later dates still see something unexpected. Taylor Swift had bespoke outfits and surprise songs during her mammoth Eras tour, Sabrina Carpenter performed unique positions during her song Juno and switched up her Nonsense outro, and Jay-Z has been changing up his set list on his current run.But the Guardian's deputy music editor Laura Snapes says it's not just fans who can benefit from these twists. "One way that they can make sure they're staying in the press is by having something different happen in their show every night," Snapes says. "Obviously, it'll be all over TikTok."Figures shared by TikTok with Newsbeat show posts using #CharliXCX have increased by more than 40% since the singer launched her Music, Fashion, Film tour last month. If you want to avoid spoilers, there's only one thing you can do, according to Snapes: "You have to not look at TikTok."If you want to be surprised, you have to protect yourself from absorbing any of that culture."Image source, Getty Images for AEGImage caption, Have you ever tried this one? Sabrina Carpenter had a number of special reveals for each show on her Short n' Sweet tourPhoebe Bridgers is taking things one step further to make sure fans are surprised at her shows - she's banning phones altogether.Those attending are required to lock their phones and any recording devices in a special pouch when they enter the venue to see the US singer. Anyone found breaking the rules will be escorted out. McAdam wouldn't support a ban on phones, saying recording at gigs is "part of the experience" for a lot of fans.But Collins says she's "not totally against it".What she'd prefer is to see more spoiler warnings on videos so fans have the option to be surprised if they want.But even if you know the set list, the staging and the outfits, "you're still probably going to get to see moments of humanity and stuff that's unplanned," Snapes adds. "I went to the Edinburgh Eras show where Taylor Swift was really snotty and she had to blow her nose. That's not part of the script."You're always going to be surprised."Listen to Newsbeat live at 12:45 and 17:45 weekdays - or listen back here.

schema.headline: Spoilers: Is social media ruining gig surprises?

title: North Macedonia 0-2 Scotland: Two going on four, five or six on good night for new era
description: Figure caption, Highlights: North Macedonia 0-2 ScotlandByBBC Scotland's chief sports writer in SkopjeWhen Scott McKenna was sent off late in the nigh
body: Figure caption, Highlights: North Macedonia 0-2 ScotlandByBBC Scotland's chief sports writer in SkopjeWhen Scott McKenna was sent off late in the night in Skopje, North Macedonia did something they looked entirely incapable of doing for 80-plus minutes spent buried in Scotland's collective pocket.They strung a couple of passes together, had a few shots, raised an odd cheer from their dismally small support. Fair play to them because for much of this Nations League game it looked as if they were comatose; out-played and out-fought. Scotland, with their energy and urgency, had reduced them to the ranks of the lifeless.Skopje is a city of statues, two or three hundred of them apparently, great big things in squares and in fountains commemorating tsars and dames, emperors and warriors, royalty and revolutionaries.  You could have taken any 11 of them off their perch and put them in the North Macedonia starting line-up and they'd have posed Scotland more of a challenge than the beleaguered home team managed for most of this encounter.At one point in the first half a dog ran on to the pitch. They'd have been better off putting a shirt on his back. At least he'd have had some bite.The scoreline does a terrible job in capturing what happened. Scotland had 25 shots to nine, 10 on target to zero. Before McKenna walked, they had touched the ball 37 times in North Macedonia's penalty area, North Macedonia had touched it twice in Scotland's.On the night that Andy Robertson won his 100th cap, this was one of his most straightforward matches of all. A stroll. A rout, if two goals can be called a rout. Two going on four and five, maybe six on what was a poor pitch in a soulless stadium, save for the visiting fans, who made a racket, as ever. It was a good evening for the new era.Scotland were exciting, entertaining and also frustrating. They had ambition but not enough execution. They created chance upon chance but didn't have the killer touch nearly as often as you'd like. That might come as things progress. Certainly, a burden was lifted off the head coach, Sebastien Pocognoli. No more chat about the search for the elusive goal, no more of that creeping negativity as he waited for a first win. The air is a touch lighter for him now as he prepares for Slovenia at Hampden on Tuesday.It was a big occasion for Robertson the centurion; a major achievement in the career of Kieron Bowie, who rifled in a terrific early goal that settled everyone down; a memorable experience for Luis Binks, Stephen Welsh and the substitute Robbie Ure, who now know what it feels like not just to play for their country but to win for their country. Binks and Welsh look at home in that Scotland defence.Decisions to make for Gannon-Doak?There was a strong sense from the start that everything would be OK for Scotland and it came in the shape of the Duracell Bunny that was the captain. Robertson began like a dervish. A shot after five minutes, then another and another and another. Four shots in 13 minutes - he's never had four shots in 90 minutes in any one of his 99 caps before Saturday.There was positivity for Scotland from early on.They had six shots in 15 minutes, the most picture-perfect of them being Bowie's strike. Oli McBurnie did some work beforehand - his wait for a goal goes on, 19 caps and counting - then the wonderful Billy Gilmour got involved. Is Gilmour a six or an eight? The truth is that he's both, a tempo-setter when dropping deep, a dangerous passer when moving forward, a complete footballer at the peak of his powers.Then it was all about Bowie. His footwork did for a defender, his accuracy did for a goalkeeper. It was a rare moment of precision in front of goal, another illustration that despite their issues in scoring goals, Scotland have a promising array of strikers these days. Time, and the confidence of this victory, should make them better.Figure caption, Pocognoli on 'special' moment for RobertsonBen Gannon-Doak turned North Macedonia inside out and upside down. He is woefully short of minutes for his club, Bournemouth, and lacks sharpness and ruthlessness as a consequence. His delivery has always lacked accuracy. His raw materials, though, are exhilarating. His pace, his involvement, his number of touches, his chances.He never left North Macedonia alone. They survived only because he blasted over with one of his chances, shot tamely with another, lost composure with a third one. Having tormented North Macedonia, he allowed them off the hook, but he was a one-man thrill-fest.He's 20, that can't be forgotten. He's going to be around for a lot of years and will play a heap of big games, but with his club he's got some decisions to make. Two minutes against Liverpool, 19 against Sociedad, eight against Brentford, one minute against Newcastle and Man City. The only game he has started this season was a League Cup tie against Lincoln.Bournemouth is a tough team to get into, but he needs more time on the grass, more opportunity to develop. Maybe a loan move in January would make sense for him, if his club allows him to go. A big 'if'. That's a situation Gannon-Doak needs to resolve for himself - and for Scotland.Figure caption, 'It's been a pleasure to stand alongside him' - McGinn on captain RobboThe chances flowed - one thunderbolt from the influential John McGinn, one near-miss from Bowie after excellence from Gannon-Doak, one off a post from McKenna. A second came via the penalty. McGinn lashed it home and drew alongside Lawrie Reilly on the all-time list - 22 and counting. After some indifferent performances, that one would have meant an awful lot to him, a strike to silence some mild questioning of his impact, a goal to put the confidence back in him, if it ever left.Pocognoli has something to build on now, three points to go with that strong second half against Slovenia a week ago; new players, aggressive football, a bit of buzz. North Macedonia were hopeless but it hardly matters. They were put away comfortably. In this series of footballing sprints, there's just one of the original four games to go now - Tuesday at Hampden. Promising signs but so much still left to do.Get in touchSend your views on the Scotland football team

title: Why thousands of couples are choosing Scotland to say 'I do'
description: Chihon Ley Polanco, from Chile, and Ana-Maria Bucatari, from Moldova, came to Scotland to study, but the country quickly became the backdrop to their
body: Chihon Ley Polanco, from Chile, and Ana-Maria Bucatari, from Moldova, came to Scotland to study, but the country quickly became the backdrop to their love story.The couple first met in 2018 through a dance society at the University of Edinburgh, when Ana-Maria was on an Erasmus exchange and Chihon was completing his postgraduate studies.They they spent years as friends, and it was not until Ana-Maria returned to Edinburgh in 2024 that their relationship became something more. And their romance blossomed in the same place their friendship had years earlier."Everything happened again on the dance floor," Ana-Maria said.Just four months after getting engaged, the pair walked down the aisle on the Isle of Arran.The couple said they "fell in love" with the island at first sight, due to it having the "complete scenery of Scotland". "You feel that you're in a magical place", said Chihon. "It's very unique."The couple said Scotland felt like the natural choice."We're from two different continents," Chihon said. "Scotland is where we met and where we built our life together."

schema.headline: Why thousands of couples are choosing Scotland to say 'I do'

title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it
description: Figure caption, How much is in your savings account?ByCost of living correspondentIf buying your own home is the finishing line, then saving up the mo
body: Figure caption, How much is in your savings account?ByCost of living correspondentIf buying your own home is the finishing line, then saving up the money to get there is a marathon.The "Your First Home" scheme, announced on Saturday, aims to help first-time buyers in England get on the housing ladder with a small deposit.Currently a 5% deposit on the average UK house price of £272,000 plus moving costs and legal fees - will set you back about £16,850, according to financial information service Moneyfacts.That's daunting, but here are four ways that experts say you can at least make a start on saving for a deposit.1. Make saving like a billDepositing an amount you can afford into a regular savers account the day after you are paid is a good way to start, suggests Anna Bowes, savings expert at financial advisers The Private Office."It becomes like another bill, but one that you can benefit from in the future," she says.The type of account that's suitable depends on your circumstances.Some of the ones that pay the highest interest  are only accessible if you hold a current account with the provider, she says.Other considerations are whether you can lock the money away for longer, to receive a better savings rate.If you don't have a buffer of other savings, then experts say an easy access account gives you the chance to dip into the money to pay an unexpected bill.2. You could get £1,000 a year You can save up to £4,000 a year in a Lifetime Individual Savings Account (LISA) and the government guarantees a 25% bonus. So, if you put the full amount in then the government will add £1,000 a year. But there is a catch, that has left some people out of pocket. Money saved in a LISA can only be used to buy a first home up to the value of £450,000 - a threshold that has not changed since 2017. The only other time you can withdraw the money is after the age of 60 or in the exceptional case that you are terminally ill with less than 12 months to live.Withdrawal under any other circumstances means you get hit with a penalty - so you could get back less than you put in.Ministers are planning to replace the LISA with a new First Time Buyer ISA, but there are no clear details yet about how it will work.3. Start earlyThe earlier you start saving the more you can build up thanks to the magic of compound interest. In short, interest is added on a larger and larger pot as time goes by.Bowes says that saving £50 a month from the age of 20 would give you about £41,000 in 30 years' time when you hit 50, assuming interest of 5% is paid a year.Start 10 years later, and you'd need to save more than double - £101 a month - to have the same amount at the age of 50.Investing in stocks and shares is another option, but the value of investments can go down as well as up.4. Save lessAn increasing number of lenders are offering mortgage deals with little or no deposit required.David Hollingworth, from L&C, points to mortgages that have deposits starting from £5,000 and allow people to borrow up to 98% or 99% of the property purchase price.They might not always be the best option, and not everyone will be eligible.And, of course, some first-time buyers turn to their parents for help. Again that's not available to all, but a survey by the Nationwide Building Society suggests that more than half of parents who charge their adult children rent are putting some or all of the money towards helping their child save to buy their own home.Get in touchAre you trying to get on to the property ladder? Share your experience. Get our flagship newsletter with all the headlines you need to start the day. Sign up here.

title: Conservatives pledge to scrap £100,000 childcare 'cliff edge'
description: The Conservatives have promised to scrap the "absurd cliff edge" that mean parents in England lose out on childcare support when they earn more than £
body: The Conservatives have promised to scrap the "absurd cliff edge" that mean parents in England lose out on childcare support when they earn more than £100,000 a year.Under the current system, only families where no parent earns more than this threshold are eligible for government-funded or tax-free childcare."What we want to see is that people who work harder don't get punished for doing so," Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme.The announcement comes as Conservative members gather for the party's annual conference in Birmingham.The party said the move would be a "first step" in broader efforts to address issues in the tax system which damage incentives to work or invest.This will be a theme of shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith's conference speech on Monday.Since September 2025, working parents in England have been entitled to 30 hours of free childcare, external for children aged between nine months and four years old.However, to qualify both parents must earn less than £100,000 a year.The same £100,000 threshold applies to the government's tax-free childcare scheme, external.For every £8 paid into an online childcare account, the government adds £2, up to £2,000 per child per year, which parents can then use to pay for childcare.The Tories said they would remove the £100,000 threshold entirely so parents no longer lose childcare support when their income exceeds this level.The threshold has been criticised by economists, who point out it can leave parents worse off overall even after a pay rise of tens of thousands of pounds.Badenoch told the BBC the party didn't want "people to stop working because of that".Speaking before the party's conference, she added: "What we want to see is more people in work and not taking the wrong decisions or the wrong choices, and it doesn't matter whether they're earning £10,000 or £100,000 - what matters is that people are out there working".Asked if this could result in someone who earns £1 million a year get free childcare under a Conservative government, Badenoch responded: "It doesn't matter what you earn - we don't want you to be punished for working hard. What we're trying to do is grow our economy."The Tories argue the threshold may mean some people may delay having children until their incomes change, or decide not to start a family at all, describing scrapping it as "both pro-family and pro-growth".By providing an increased incentive to work, the Tories said the move would also boost economic growth.They added that it would tackle the "unfairness" that the threshold is calculated on an individual earner's income rather then for the whole household.In a statement, Griffith said: "Removing this childcare cliff edge is the first step in our mission to deliver lower, simpler, and fairer taxes across the board."The party said the policy would be funded by cutting the number of public servants working in "executive non-departmental public bodies" - organisations which have a role in the processes of national government but operate at arm's length from ministers, such as Arts Council England and the Environment Agency.It said this would save £1.6bn by 2029-30, covering the estimated £700 million cost of removing the childcare "cliff edge".Badenoch arrived in Birmingham on Saturday ahead of the annual conference, and vowed the party was new and different from the one that lost the 2024 general election.The party - which is currently polling behind Labour and Reform UK - is expected to use the event to lay out more of its growing policy agenda ahead of the next general election.

schema.headline: Conservatives pledge to scrap £100,000 childcare 'cliff edge'

title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says
description: The co-pilot who attempted to take control of a Flydubai plane travelling to Israel attacked the pilot with a crash axe, the United Arab Emirates pros
body: The co-pilot who attempted to take control of a Flydubai plane travelling to Israel attacked the pilot with a crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said.The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv carrying more than 170 people plunged 17,000ft (5,200m) two and a half hours into its journey, before passengers managed to overpower the attacker and successfully take control of the plane.Capt Smit Machchhar said he was lying on the floor injured when he realised the plane was sinking and he had to act, explaining: "I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside", which allowed the passengers in.Two reserve pilots then landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia.A crash axe is usually kept ​in the cockpit in case of emergencies.The weapon used has been a key question for investigators, given the stringent security on such a sensitive route. Early reports from passengers on board had suggested it might have been a knife.The UAE attorney general told state media that investigations were ongoing to determine the full circumstances and motives of the incident.The co-pilot who launched the attack was an Omani national, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Multiple media outlets including Reuters, CNN and The New York Times have named him as Hamam al-Hammami. There has been no official confirmation of this.While working at another airline, Oman Air, US media reported that Al-Hammami was removed from flight training because of concerns over his radical views, and was given another role at Oman's national airline.He completed a three-year distance-learning course at Buckinghamshire New University in the UK and graduated with a degree in aviation management in 2023, the university said. It added he did not take any pilot training at the school.Speaking to Fox News, Netanyahu said that after the attacker was subdued on the flight, he called out to the crew "Kill me, kill me!"The Israeli prime minister added: "So, it's clear that he was suicidal… It looks very likely that he was going to down the plane."He also said the attacker "underwent Islamist radical indoctrination".The UAE's attorney general, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, said investigations into the incident revealed that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a "terrorist act", according to the country's state news agency.He also said investigations were under way to establish the circumstances, motives and any links related to the incident.Machchhar, who was stabbed in the attack, was taken to a nearby hospital before being airlifted to Abu Dhabi, where he is reported to be in a stable condition.The pilot, who is from India, was in "good health and recovering well", the Indian embassy in the UAE said on Thursday."I am confident that the recovery will be there and I will become fit and healthy again," Machchhar said.About two and half hours after the plane took off from Dubai International Airport it begun to plunge sharply. The plane signalled a "general emergency" code, squawk 7700, before switching to squawk 7500, a code reporting "unlawful interference", or hijacking.In an interview with the BBC, one passenger described the moment he realised that something was wrong.Almog Itali said: "Suddenly the aeroplane started to, like a rollercoaster, to drop down [with] a massive G-force. It was falling down for 20 or 30 seconds, rapidly, and then balanced, and then started once again to fall down."People then began to rush to the cockpit, he said.Israeli President Isaac Herzog said on Thursday that the alarm was raised onboard by an Israeli woman, Tali Manes, who heard a commotion coming from the cockpit. Her husband, Zvika, along with three other men - Yaniv Hayun, Dr Shota Musayev and Asaf Rajuan - entered the cockpit after Capt Machchhar managed to open the door despite his injuries. Hayun said, in a video released by the prime minister's office, that the attacker was "trying to destroy the instruments in order to disable the plane".Hayun then described putting the attacker in a chokehold and pulling him outside the cockpit before other passengers helped to pin him down.He added that he "pulled the controls" of the plane. "The plane started to level out, a bit more, and then [another] pilot told me he was taking control from there," he said.In an interview with CNN on Wednesday evening, Netanyahu said the stabbed pilot, passengers and second crew had "managed to prevent a 9/11 disaster".

schema.headline: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says

title: Protesters across Spain demand action over housing crisis
description: One of the biggest demonstration is happening in the capital, Madrid. Estimates of the number of participants varied widely, with the city's Tenants'
body: One of the biggest demonstration is happening in the capital, Madrid. Estimates of the number of participants varied widely, with the city's Tenants' Union putting it at 500,000, while government officials put the figure at 70,000.Demonstrators held banners reading "There won't be peace for rentism" and "I study to have a future, not to have a tiny apartment". They shook the keys they were holding and chanted: "We have the keys of all the city".Some have also been camping in one of the city's main squares, Puerta del Sol, for days.One protester, David, told RTVE ahead of the protest: "We're not here for pleasure or comfort. We're here out of conviction."Another protester, 26-year-old librarian Marcos Sainz, told AFP news agency that he used to share a two-bedroom flat with friends, paying 900 euros (£766) a month in rent. Today, he said a one-bedroom flat often costs 1,000 euros.Sainz said he would protest against rent rises "until someone dares to regulate it all", or "we'll all have to leave Madrid".On Friday night, Madrid's Tenants' Union said that although the government's proposed measures were insufficient, the rejection of the proposed legislation "exacerbates the housing crisis which is costing the working class their lives".It is calling for a general strike over the housing crisis.The legislation put forward in Congress on Friday was divided into two separate decrees.The first decree included the suspension of evictions of vulnerable tenants until 2030, a two-year extension to rental leases due to expire before 2028, tax increases for tourist apartments, and a restriction on the purchase of residential properties by  so-called "vulture funds".The second decree included the automatic renewal of rental contracts, a major demand of many on the left and the Tenants' Union.MPs rejected the first decree by 178 votes to 172 and voted against the second by 184 to 166.Prior to the vote, the conservative People's Party (PP) and far-right Vox had already said they would vote against both initiatives, leaving the minority government depending on the support of smaller nationalist parties in Catalonia and the Basque Country.However, by the eve of the parliamentary session, the centre-right, pro-independence Together for Catalonia (JxCat) had signalled its opposition to both laws, condemning them to failure.Sánchez's ruling coalition hurriedly drew up the decree laws in an effort to defuse the housing protests that were sparked when 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal was evicted in September.The social backlash led to the company that owns Abascal's flat, Urbagestión, negotiating her return to the flat on a low rent. However, protests have continued.

schema.headline: Protesters across Spain demand action over housing crisis

title: Tennessee prison chief to resign after Christa Pike's failed execution
description: The head of prisons in the US state of Tennessee is resigning after the failed execution of death row inmate Christa Pike on Wednesday. Governor Bill
body: The head of prisons in the US state of Tennessee is resigning after the failed execution of death row inmate Christa Pike on Wednesday. Governor Bill Lee announced the change on Saturday, sharing the news in a joint statement with Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada.Strada said that his stepping down is "in the best interests" of the state, and called the ongoing investigation into the incident "entirely appropriate and necessary".Pike, who was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer, survived two injections and is now in critical condition at a Tennessee hospital as her lawyers seek to commute her sentence."Commissioner Strada has served with integrity, and I appreciate his willingness to put the interests of Tennesseans first during this difficult moment," Lee said. Lee has ordered an independent review into Pike's attempted execution and he halted all executions in the state for the year.Attorneys for Pike called the resignation "justified" but said "it does nothing to help Christa now"."What happened to her Wednesday reflects a systemic failure that goes far beyond any one person," Pike's legal team wrote in a statement. "We hope the Governor's call for a full, independent review will expose the profound problems within Tennessee's entire death penalty system."Pike is being treated at a hospital in Nashville, Tennessee, where doctors are attempting to clear the drugs used during the execution from her body, according to legal filings. She was injected with two lethal doses of pentobarbital on Wednesday but remained alive. She was then sent to hospital in an ambulance. While receiving the two doses, "she could be heard crying, whimpering, and breathing loudly throughout the procedure", her lawyers said.As of Thursday night, she was unconscious, intubated and on a ventilator. The state's Department of Correction has defended the method it used, saying "the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out".Authorities have not yet said whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have also not offered an explanation for what went wrong. Her lawyers filed an emergency motion on Friday to preserve "any and all evidence" related to her failed execution.Pike's attorneys previously warned that her medical history and anatomy - including thrombocytosis (a blood-clotting condition) and small veins - meant there was a risk she would experience "unnecessary" pain and suffering during a lethal injection.The attempted execution went ahead after multiple failed, last-minute legal challenges by Pike's lawyers.The US Supreme Court rejected two separate efforts to stop the lethal injection.Tennessee's governor also denied a clemency request from Pike, the only woman on the state's death row.Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer in 1995.She was sentenced to death the following year after a media frenzy around the killing in Knoxville, Tennessee.

schema.headline: Tennessee prison chief to resign after Christa Pike's failed execution

title: Homemade bomb part of alleged plot on Manchester's Jewish community, court told
description: Two Iranian men have appeared in court charged with terror offences over an alleged plot to target the Jewish community in Manchester with a homemade
body: Two Iranian men have appeared in court charged with terror offences over an alleged plot to target the Jewish community in Manchester with a homemade bomb. Rahman Salehi, 34, of Salford, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, from Liverpool, were accused at Westminster Magistrates' Court of preparing to commit an act of terrorism or assisting another to commit an act of terrorism on or before 20 September.One of the buildings they are alleged to have carried out reconnaissance at is the Heaton Park synagogue which was attacked on 2 October 2025.Both men, who had arrived in the UK by small boat, were arrested in Manchester's Northern Quarter on the eve of Yom Kippur - the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.Salehi and Ahmadyan were remanded in custody by District Judge Nina Tempia until 23 October, when they will appear at the Old Bailey in London.As part of the investigation, searches were carried out at addresses in Epworth Street, Liverpool, and Lancaster Road, Salford.The Metropolitan Police said the men were alleged to have obtained instructions to make a chlorine bomb, acquired liquids and other components to make an improvised explosive device.They are accused of using the internet to identify and research potential targets, acquiring images, plans and maps.Prosecutor Mark Luckett told the court: "Both defendants are accused of preparing acts of terrorism targeting the Jewish community in Manchester through the use of a homemade explosive device."The defendants were observed carrying out, what the prosecution say, is a hostile reconnaissance within Manchester's Jewish community, identifying attempted targets such as the Jewish Museum and Heaton Park Synagogue."Two British Jews, Melvin Kravitz, 66, and 53-year-old Adrian Daulby, were killed when Heaton Park Synagogue was attacked during last year's Yom Kippur service.Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, drove into the gates of Heaton Park Hebrew Synagogue and began attacking people with a knife while wearing a fake suicide belt.Westminster Magistrates' Court court heard Salehi and Ahmadyan, who had come to the UK via a small boat in 2020 and 2023 respectively, were alleged to have been "directed and co-ordinated" by another Iranian individual "most likely operating within Iran".Salehi had previously claimed asylum in Germany and spent five years there, the court heard. He was granted asylum in the UK in 2023 and currently has leave to remain until July 2028.His co-accused arrived via small boat in 2023 and has an outstanding asylum claim, the court heard.The men, wearing grey tracksuits, stood in the dock of court five.Salehi and Ahmadyan respectively spoke through their Kurdish and Farsi translators only to confirm their name, date of birth and addresses.Prior to their court appearance, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the news that two Iranian men had been charged would be "deeply distressing" to Manchester's Jewish community as the city marked the first anniversary of the Heaton Park Synagogue attack.She said "the fact both suspects arrived by small boat several years ago" was a reminder of the "importance of work to tackle illegal migration"."We will be unrelenting in our efforts to protect our Jewish communities, root out antisemitism in this country, and maintain our border security," she added.

schema.headline: Homemade bomb part of alleged plot on Manchester's Jewish community, court told

title: England player ratings v Croatia: Who was the best player on the pitch?
description: Jordan Pickford: A really good decision and save when he raced out and won the ball at the feet of Ivan Perisic early on. Not tested but was lucky to
body: Jordan Pickford: A really good decision and save when he raced out and won the ball at the feet of Ivan Perisic early on. Not tested but was lucky to not concede with Mateo Kovacic's incredible miss. 6Jarell Quansah: Surprisingly chosen at right-back over Trent Alexander-Arnold but the Bayer Leverkusen defender does exactly what manager Thomas Tuchel wants. A powerful runner, a good defender and his ability on the ball is underrated - he showed it with a quality assist for Gordon. 8Ezri Konsa: Not loads of defending for Konsa to do as England pinned Croatia back but it was a calm assured performance from the defender. 7Marc Guehi: The centre-back had to take up some risky positions as England pressed man for man all over the pitch. 7Lewis Hall: The Newcastle left-back looks a great addition to the England back four. Hall offers pace going forward and also underlapped, going into midfield to recieve the ball. 7 Elliot Anderson: Anderson has been excellent throughout this international break and produced another mature performance. The Manchester City midfielder is a crucial part of the midfield and set up Kane for England's fifth. 8Alex Scott: The Bournemouth midfielder was given his first England start and put in a really confident performance. Scott always looked to get on the ball and did not just try to keep it safe as England dominated. 7Jude Bellingham: The best player on the pitch. Bellingham produced a lovely pass to thread Kane through for the first goal, scored England's second and assisted Saka for England's fourth. A truly world-class player and his quality was too much for Croatia throughout the game. 9Bukayo Saka: The winger scored twice and looks to be building a good partnership with Quansah on England's right-hand side. Saka could have had a hat-trick but missed a big chance in the second half. 8Anthony Gordon: Playing with a huge amount of confidence and continues to show that he has gone to another level in recent months. Assisted Bellingham and scored for the fourth England game in a row. 9Harry Kane: Just an elite finisher and his goal put England firmly in control. The captain looked full of energy, pressed from the front and showed his passing range as he enjoyed having Gordon and Bellingham supplying him. Scored England's fifth goal too. 9

schema.headline: England player ratings v Croatia: Who was the best player on the pitch?
